name: cloud_sheet_lapse
description:
§25's cloud sheets MOVING, which is the only way to judge them — a still frame cannot show whether a sky drifts or slides, and the whole design (bounded sheets at varying speeds, entering and leaving off-map) exists to answer that. ALL THREE LANES ON, so what is filmed is one cloud deck seen three ways — the sheet above, its shadow on the ground, and (at dusk) the light it bounces down — all sharing one CloudSheetLayout, which is the property these films exist to show. Two TickLapse sweeps on the same tile and season as cloud_layers.json: partly cloudy Clear at noon (five sheets), then Overcast at noon (twelve), so the count-from-cloudiness rule can be seen rather than read.

TICKS, NOT HOURS, and that is the whole reason this is a separate scenario from cloud_underlight_layer_lapse.json. Sheet placement is a function of the absolute tick, and one crossing takes CloudSheetLayout.BaseCrossingTicks (20000, most of an in-game day). A Timelapse's hour steps would jump most of a crossing per frame and read as teleporting; 30 ticks a frame over 240 frames covers roughly a third of one crossing smoothly, which is what motion looks like. The step size was raised alongside BaseCrossingTicks: slowing the clouds and keeping the film's step fixed would have filmed the same span at half the motion.

No pins: this exists to be watched, and every number worth asserting is already pinned in cloud_layers.json.
